subjectLine: BREAKING: Attackers Exploit CVSS 10.0 Bricksforge WordPress Flaw Enabl + More Inside
weekIntro: This week's operational threat landscape is dominated by perimeter appliance compromises, led by active exploitation of a maximum-severity flaw in SonicWall gateways and an out-of-band zero-day patch for Microsoft Exchange. Meanwhile, core infrastructure teams must urgently address root-level remote code execution across Cisco Nexus switches and extensive patch rollouts for enterprise Linux deployments. DevOps and security teams also face renewed supply-chain pressure as automated credential-harvesting campaigns target GitHub Actions workflows and npm packages.

articles.title: GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability
articles.summary: GitLab warned users to immediately patch a maximum‑severity vulnerability in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler that could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances.

articles.title: Attackers Exploit CVSS 10.0 Bricksforge WordPress Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
articles.summary: A maximum‑severity security flaw impacting the Bricksforge plugin for WordPress is being actively exploited in the wild, according to Patchstack. The critical vulnerability (CVE‑…) allows unauthenticated remote code execution.

articles.title: SonicWall Issues Hotfix for Critical CVE‑2026‑102255 SSRF in SMA1000 Appliances as Exploits Appear in the Wild
articles.summary: SonicWall released patches for four critical flaws in SMA1000 gateways, with CVE‑2026‑102255—a pre‑authentication SSRF in the WorkPlace portal—rated 10.0 CVSS. Within days of release, threat‑monitoring honeypots observed exploitation attempts targeting internal CouchDB services, confirming active abuse of the vulnerability.
articles.impact: Unauthenticated attackers can force the appliance to issue internal requests, potentially accessing sensitive services and executing unauthorized operations on any exposed SMA1000 device.
articles.action: Apply the SonicWall hotfix (12.4.3‑03670 or later, 12.5.0‑03082 or later) immediately and verify the appliance restarts successfully.

articles.title: Microsoft Issues Out‑of‑Band Patch for Critical Exchange Server Privilege‑Escalation Flaw (CVE‑2026‑96940)
articles.summary: Microsoft released an out‑of‑band update for CVE‑2026‑96940, a high‑severity Exchange Server vulnerability that lets authenticated attackers elevate privileges and read other users' mailboxes within the same organization. The flaw is actively exploited, carries an 8.8 CVSS score, and affects multiple on‑premises Exchange versions.
articles.impact: Security teams must assume that any compromised credential could be used to harvest internal email traffic, exposing sensitive communications and attachments. The vulnerability does not cross tenant boundaries but can compromise every mailbox on an affected server.
articles.action: Apply the October 2, 2026 Exchange Server security updates immediately to all affected on‑premises installations.
affected_systems: Microsoft Exchange Server Subscription Edition RTM

articles.title: Cisco Issues Critical NX‑OS Advisories for Five Root‑Level Exploits
articles.summary: Cisco disclosed five critical vulnerabilities in NX‑OS that allow remote code execution with root privileges on Nexus 3000 and Nexus 9000 switches. Exploits target NX‑API, Next‑Generation OAM, and MPLS OAM when those features are enabled, potentially enabling full device takeover or denial‑of‑service.
articles.impact: Compromised switches can give attackers unrestricted control over data‑center traffic, manipulate VLANs, or disrupt services, exposing the entire fabric to breach or outage.
articles.action: Apply the latest Cisco patches immediately and disable any unused NX‑API, NGOAM, or MPLS OAM features until the fixes are in place.

articles.title: Researchers Release Working Exploit for Pre‑Auth AnyDesk Linux RCE, Patching Required
articles.summary: A functional exploit named AnyPwn targets a heap buffer overflow in AnyDesk Linux 8.0.2, granting unauthenticated root access over direct TCP port 7070. AnyDesk patched the flaw in version 8.0.
articles.impact: Unpatched AnyDesk Linux clients can be fully compromised before any user interaction, exposing critical infrastructure to remote takeover.
articles.action: Upgrade all AnyDesk Linux installations to version 8.0.3 or later immediately.

articles.title: GhostAction Supply‑Chain Attack Injects Credential‑Stealing GitHub Actions Workflows into 340+ Repositories
articles.summary: Researchers uncovered a credential‑theft campaign that compromised two high‑profile maintainer accounts to push malicious GitHub Actions workflows into more than 340 open‑source repositories, exfiltrating over 3,300 secrets—including AWS, OpenAI, and DockerHub tokens—to a hard‑coded IP via plain HTTP.
articles.impact: Security teams face immediate risk of secret leakage from CI pipelines and downstream services, and the compromised workflows can persist across thousands of downstream forks.
articles.action: Audit all recent workflow changes, revoke and rotate exposed secrets, and enforce least‑privilege PATs with MFA for all GitHub maintainer accounts.

articles.title: Red Hat Releases Broad Patch Update for RHEL, OpenShift, and Core Services
articles.summary: Red Hat released a batch of Critical and Important security advisories across Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, OpenShift Container Platform, and foundational enterprise packages.
articles.impact: Unpatched enterprise infrastructure faces risks of unauthorized root compromise, remote code execution, container escapes, and compromised authentication services across production environments. Critical enterprise workloads, including SAP Solutions and containerized control planes, are directly vulnerable until patched.
articles.action: Audit exposed hosts and cluster nodes, apply updated errata packages and kernel builds immediately, and roll out updates to OpenShift deployments.

articles.title: Tensorlake npm SDK Compromised in ChainDrop/Shai‑Hulud Supply‑Chain Attack Delivering Credential‑Stealing Worm
articles.summary: The Tensorlake TypeScript SDK (npm package “tensorlake” version 0.5.144) was backdoored by the ChainDrop/Shai‑Hulud group. The malicious release installs a pre‑install hook that runs an obfuscated Bun‑based loader, harvesting npm, GitHub, AWS, Vault, Kubernetes, SSH, .
articles.impact: Security teams face immediate risk of credential theft across CI pipelines, cloud environments, and secret stores, and attackers can retain access even after the tainted package is removed.
articles.action: Remove version 0.5.144, audit all systems for leaked credentials, rotate secrets, and monitor for unauthorized package publications.

articles.title: FBI Confirms FortiBleed Credential Harvesting Campaign Remains Active on FortiGate Firewalls and SSL VPNs
articles.summary: The FBI and Secret Service warned that the FortiBleed operation continues to harvest credentials from internet‑exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, exploiting reused or leaked passwords stored with...
articles.impact: Security teams face ongoing risk of unauthorized access to perimeter devices, enabling persistent footholds and lateral movement across networks.
articles.action: Immediately enforce phishing‑resistant authentication, terminate active VPN and admin sessions, reset all Fortinet passwords, switch to PBKDF2 for credential storage, and review logs for suspicious activity.

articles.title: Critical LMCache Remote Code Execution Flaw Exposes Unauthenticated Attackers via ZeroMQ
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in LMCache (versions 0.3.9 through 0.5.5, including 0.5.6 RCs) allows unauthenticated remote code execution through a crafted ZeroMQ message that exploits unsafe pickle deserialization.
articles.impact: Any LMCache instance listening on a non‑localhost interface can be hijacked, executing attacker‑supplied code with the privileges of the LMCache process and potentially compromising the host running LLM workloads.
articles.action: Immediately reconfigure LMCache to bind only to localhost or restrict network access, apply strict firewall rules, and monitor for suspicious ZeroMQ traffic while awaiting a patched release.

articles.title: Hackers Issue Counterfeit TLS Certificates for Google and Other Major Services via Compromised ccTLD Registries
articles.summary: Attackers hijacked the .gh, .sl, and .as country‑code top‑level domains, altered DNS records, and passed domain‑validation checks to obtain unauthorized TLS certificates for multiple Google domains and other high‑profile services.
articles.impact: The breach enables man‑in‑the‑middle attacks that can decrypt traffic and impersonate affected sites, exposing users and internal systems to credential theft and data exfiltration.
articles.action: Security teams must continuously monitor certificate transparency logs for unexpected issuances and enforce restrictive CA authorization policies.

articles.title: Ubuntu Patches AMD SEV-SNP Memory Isolation Flaw in Linux Kernel
articles.summary: Canonical released Linux kernel security updates addressing CVE-2023-20585, a flaw where AMD processors fail to enforce Reverse Map Table checks during IOMMU accesses to host buffers.
articles.impact: Malicious or compromised hypervisors can bypass hardware-enforced memory encryption and integrity checks. This invalidates confidential computing isolation guarantees for workloads running in multi-tenant environments.
articles.action: Apply the latest Linux kernel updates released in USN-8887-3 to all affected Ubuntu host systems and reboot.
